title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating failed episodes as failures/regressions) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015, exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25; the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for this sensitivity is reproducible from the archived per‑pair raw_results (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using the preregistered seed and resample counts (see Reproducibility). Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide explicit artifact pointers and checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) promise to translate high‑level operator intent into device configurations and to assist network operations (NetOps) at scale. Operational NetOps requires not only syntactic plausibility but demonstrable functional correctness, bounded blast radius (i.e., limited collateral impact), and auditability. A commonly proposed architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM generates a candidate configuration; a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants and policy constraints; an automated repair subroutine attempts to correct violations (possibly iteratively). Prior work motivates verifier use and tool‑assisted correction (e.g., CRITIC, intent engines, and NetOps verifiers), but there is limited preregistered paired evidence isolating the verifier effect with complete provenance. We ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) and executed it end‑to‑end with archival of inputs, outputs, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: Relevant threads include intent→configuration translation and LLM→IaC generation (PreConfig, intent engines), generate‑and‑validate architectures and LLM self‑correction (CRITIC and tool‑assisted critiquing), and deterministic NetOps verifiers (SymNet and ensemble verification). These works motivate verifier‑guided pipelines but rarely provide preregistered, within‑task paired inference isolating the verifier’s causal effect with full artifact release. Surveys and recent NetOps LLM studies document architectural desiderata (auditability, verifier coverage, repair budgets) and point to ceiling effects when baseline LLM correctness is high. Our contribution is a preregistered within‑task paired evaluation focused on operational functional correctness with deterministic provenance and explicit accounting of repair invocations and missingness.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified a paired confirmatory design. Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline). The preregistered primary hypothesis (H1) required an absolute reduction in regression rate of ≥ 0.20 (i.e., Δ ≤ −0.20 for regression indicator; equivalent prespecified effect size reflected in power calculations). Experimental design and task bank. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to create 200 stratified intent→golden‑config tasks constrained to constructs supported by the deterministic verifier (see task manifest execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Topology scales were stratified (small, medium, large) and vendor‑mix strata included common features (BGP, OSPF, VLAN, MTU). Inclusion/exclusion rules were automated: tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded deterministically and archived. Execution adapter and model. The adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed paired episodes using the declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). For each task a single shared initial generation was performed (shared initial candidate reused across conditions per preregistration). Guarded condition. Guarded episodes ran deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and, when violations were reported, invoked up to one automated repair call (preregistered maximum). The verifier returned structured validator traces (validation_before / validation_after) used by the repair subroutine and archived in execution/scoring/*.json entries (many representative artifact examples and checksums are provided). Analysis plan. Primary test: exact two‑sided McNemar on complete pairs with 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Missingness policy: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed) and a prespecified sensitivity analysis treating both‑missing pairs as failures ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'). The analysis executor identifier is paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis artifacts include the paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766) and an analysis log (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) recording bootstrap parameters.
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2). Completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs included in the primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12. Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). Contingency (complete pairs n = 188): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both fail in complete‑pair set). Aggregate (complete‑pair) estimates: baseline_success = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_success = 188/188 = 1.0; Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records seed and resample count). The preregistered efficacy target (absolute Δ ≥ 0.20) was not met. Sensitivity (both‑missing → failures). When both_missing pairs (12 pairs) are treated as failures per the prespecified sensitivity, N=200 and counts become n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12. Guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25 (discordant counts unchanged). The preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for this sensitivity is reproducible from the archived per‑pair raw_results (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using the preregistered seed (1729) and 10,000 resamples; the execution/analysis artifacts include deterministic raw per‑episode records required for resampling and the analysis_log.jsonl that documents the bootstrap parameters. Repair activity and mapping. Repair was invoked 3 times (stage_counts.repair = 3) and these three invocations correspond to the three guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). The execution archive contains the per‑call provider traces and the raw_results.jsonl entries that link each repair invocation to its episode_id, pair_id, provider_call filename, and final score. Representative per‑episode scoring JSONs included in the manuscript evidence (e.g., execution/scoring/task‑000001‑guarded.json, execution/scoring/task‑000002‑guarded.json, execution/scoring/task‑000003‑guarded.json) contain shared_initial_provider_trace_path values and response SHAs; the full raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) and the provider_calls directory in the archive enumerate the explicit per‑call filenames and SHA‑256 checksums for the three repair traces. Because the raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory are part of the supplied artifact bundle and their checksums are provided above, readers can deterministically extract (episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename, provider_call_sha256, final_score) for each repair invocation from the archive; the deterministic_reconciliation.json provider_call_audit block records stage_counts and call totals for cross‑checking. Blast radius & repair iterations. Repair invocations were rare (3) and the repair subroutine was limited to one automated attempt per preregistration. Consequently, we cannot robustly estimate distributions of repair iterations or provide reliable aggregate blast‑radius statistics beyond the archived per‑episode validator traces that report observed_touched_field_count and parsed_command_count for each episode (examples in execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement in success rate (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes corrected by the automated repair path. This effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and is not statistically significant. Two operational causes are visible in the archive: (1) ceiling effect—baseline correctness among complete pairs was high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and task selection—the verifier supports a constrained feature set and the sampled synthetic task family produced many LLM proposals that already matched the golden configuration or passed validation, so repairs were rarely invoked. Implications. Deterministic verifiers provide auditability and can correct some LLM mistakes; however, measurable operational benefit depends on baseline model error rates, verifier feature coverage, and task difficulty. In contexts with high initial LLM correctness, the marginal utility of verifier‑guided repair is limited unless verifier scope or repair budget is increased. Reproducibility and artifact‑grounded verification. All artifacts needed to reproduce the analysis are archived with SHA‑256 checksums. Key artifacts: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) contains the per‑episode records used for bootstrap resampling and links to provider_call filenames; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766) contains the contingency used for the primary McNemar test; deterministic_reconciliation.json contains provider call audit counts including stage_counts.repair = 3. Reproducibility recipe (deterministic). To reproduce the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for either the complete‑pair analysis or the sensitivity described above, resample pairs (with replacement) from the archived per‑pair records in execution/raw_results.jsonl, compute Δ per resample, and take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles across 10,000 resamples with seed=1729. The analysis log (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) records the exact seed and resample count. If a reader needs an exact executor invocation, the analysis executor identifier is paired_binary_analysis_v1 (the execution manifest and analysis directory in the archive include the executor entrypoints and invocation records; artifact checksums above allow deterministic extraction). Threats to validity. Internal validity: prompt sensitivity (single shared initial candidate per pair), retries limited to preregistered policy, and 24 failed episodes reduced the complete_pair sample to 188. Construct validity: the success metric is a deterministic validator‑based functional correctness indicator; it depends on verifier coverage and the fidelity of the synthetic golden configs. External validity: single‑model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic Cornetto‑like tasks, and limited verifier scope restrict generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) reduce power to detect large absolute effects compared to the preregistered assumption. Recommendations for future work. To detect verifier impact in high‑baseline settings, future studies should (a) increase baseline task difficulty or broaden verifier‑unsupported constructs in exploratory sets; (b) increase repair budgets (multiple repair iterations) and log iterative repair traces; (c) evaluate multiple LLM families and verifier implementations to assess generality; (d) report per‑call blast‑radius distributions derived from validator traces (observed_touched_field_count) for operational cost accounting.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; however high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, model ensembles, and repair budgets.

This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 but was not recomputed inline in the printed manuscript because the drafting snapshot did not contain a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the supplied snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the above checksum.
